text: {"distance_m": 1.5, "reasoning_short": "Rough estimate. A 1 mm, 15%-contrast spot is a tiny low-contrast target, so its limit is set by contrast × area, not by 20/20 letter acuity (1 arcmin). Blackwell-type threshold data suggest it needs to span about 2–2.5 arcmin (about 6–7×10⁻⁴ rad) to be seen. That gives 1 mm / 6.5×10⁻⁴ ≈ 1.5–1.7 m. Indoor light is dimmer than those test conditions, so ~1.5 m is the better figure."}
